feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy-heavy roles. Writing is polished overall, but the document is slightly repetitive and would be stronger with more outcome-focused metrics and tighter consolidation of overlapping skills sections.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, showing increasing responsibility from coordinator to director to consultant.  
- Strong credibility through concrete scope indicators: 10,000+ page migration, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ internal publishers, and broad platform/tool expertise.  
- Professional, readable writing with a consistent leadership narrative across digital strategy, governance, content operations, and multimedia.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable impact beyond scope: include results such as traffic growth, engagement gains, email performance, cost savings, process efficiencies, or campaign outcomes.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidating these would improve structure and scannability.  
- Minor style/grammar consistency issues: add “of” in “more than 12 years of experience”; standardize serial comma usage (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement”); “cross-channel” and “multi-channel” may feel stylistically inconsistent. No obvious misspellings or major typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear positioning, but it repeats several competency phrases already covered elsewhere and could be sharper by tying the profile more directly to recent leadership and platform modernization work. Also fix “12 years experience” to “12 years’ experience” or “over 12 years of experience.”

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Lead with current seniority and niche: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience in mission-driven and public-sector organizations.”
- Replace broad channel list with higher-value outcomes: emphasize enterprise web modernization, cross-channel operations, governance, and analytics-informed strategy.
- Add a clearer differentiator from the experience section: advocacy/policy communication plus translating complex issues into accessible content.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience building and leading cross-channel programs for mission-driven organizations. Expertise includes enterprise web modernization, content operations, editorial governance, and analytics-informed strategy across web, email, social, and multimedia. Strong background in advocacy and policy communications, stakeholder alignment, and translating complex issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” closely repeat Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- The channel list duplicates multiple work-experience bullets; keep the intro higher-level.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening wording and emphasizing higher-value leadership/technical strengths will make it sharper.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic phrases with more senior, specific language: “Multi-channel communication” → “Cross-channel communications leadership”; “Web & CMS administration” → “Web platform modernization & CMS management.”
- Reduce overlap and group related items for clarity: “Editorial workflow design” + “Workflow & systems architecture” could become “Editorial operations, governance & workflow systems.”
- Prioritize strongest differentiators from recent roles: digital transformation, Drupal/web modernization, analytics infrastructure, advocacy communications, and multimedia/event production.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital transformation & communications strategy • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform modernization & CMS management • Editorial operations, governance & workflow systems • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Stakeholder and cross-functional leadership • Public-sector policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia, video & live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats themes already covered in the header and Topline Skills, especially digital strategy, advocacy messaging, analytics, and coordination.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” also overlaps with Soft Skills.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with your prior NACo entries and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consultant-level outcomes, transformation work, and what is new since returning.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancements, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery for enterprise communications.”
- Replace generic verbs with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Redesigned workflows and analytics to improve cross-team coordination” instead of “Build and refine digital systems…”
- Consolidate web/CMS bullets: combine microsites, front-end implementation, and troubleshooting into one stronger bullet focused on delivered platform improvements.
- Add measurable signals where possible: number of sites/pages supported, toolkit downloads, publishing efficiency gains, search relevance improvements, or stakeholder teams served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, usability and operational best practices” repeats themes already covered in Director of Digital Media.
- The AI search and microsite bullets may duplicate Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and reserve specifics for the project section.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more specific and measurable: include newsletter volume/open-rate growth, social engagement growth, or campaign results if available; otherwise shorten.
- Tighten operations bullets: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio” and “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting to improve executive decision-making” and “Established governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this version focused on enterprise leadership and scale.
- Video-programming language overlaps with older NACo entries; emphasize studio buildout, not recurring production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong mid-career progression item with clear channel ownership, but it reads a bit generic and overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Tighten it around scope, cadence, and what changed under your leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize execution ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, supporting coordinated advocacy and member communications.”
- Make bullets more outcome-focused: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Sharpen the video bullet: “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger line: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows by coordinating communications, advocacy and program teams around more consistent digital production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations” overlaps with the Director of Digital Media entry; keep this role more execution-focused, less enterprise-level.
- Weekly video/livestream language may duplicate the 2015–2018 role; frame this entry as scaling and formalizing the program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent NACo roles. It should sharpen the highest-value leadership areas and use more distinctive phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with tighter, more differentiated language:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership for web, email, social & video
- Public-sector, membership & advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy & campaign planning
- Swap “messaging” for “communications” or “campaigns” to sound more senior and operational.
- Add “web modernization” and “content operations” to better reflect recent, high-impact work.
- Keep each line parallel and specific; avoid broad phrases like “audience-focused content planning” unless tied to strategy or campaigns.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate both the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” also overlaps with multiple NACo experience bullets; rephrase to emphasize scope or channel ownership.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill coverage, but this item is too tool-list-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value capabilities and recent strengths, not repeat every platform.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Remove lower-priority or older-signal items here, especially “jQuery,” unless it is central to current target roles.
- Prioritize recent, proven strengths from NACo work: Drupal, CMS modernization, integrations/workflow automation, AI-enabled search.
- If possible, make “SharePoint” and “Power Pages” secondary or move them fully to Technical + IT unless supported by recent accomplishments.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; avoid repeating the same platform list in both places.
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also overlap with Core Competencies; keep wording distinct.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack that aligns with the most recent NACo leadership role, but it reads as a generic keyword list. Tighten it around decision-making impact and avoid repeating “reporting/analytics” language already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + outcome language, e.g.:
  “GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, and BigQuery • KPI framework development • executive dashboarding • SEO, UX, and performance optimization”
- Consider replacing “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboarding” or “Decision-ready reporting” for sharper phrasing.
- Change “SEO and performance analysis” to “SEO, UX, and conversion/performance analysis” if accurate; it’s more specific and modern.
- If space allows, prioritize the most recent/high-value tools first: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity…”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Data analytics & reporting” already appears in Core Competencies; this skills line should emphasize tools and optimization focus, not repeat broad analytics language.
- Power BI/Looker Studio/BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so keep this section concise rather than restating impact claims.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it reads generic and overlaps with achievements already shown in NACo roles. Make it more senior, systems-oriented, and tied to the strongest recent evidence: studio buildout, livestreams, and hybrid event delivery.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe for scope and seniority: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event operations • Post-production editing”
- Replace “Livestreaming” with “Livestream and hybrid event delivery” to sound more outcome-focused and aligned with current market language.
- Replace “Studio operations” with “PTZ camera and studio systems” or “Studio buildout and operations” if you want to reflect the in-house studio achievement.
- If space allows, emphasize leadership over task execution: “Multimedia production leadership” or “End-to-end video and event production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section duplicates “Multimedia & live event production” in Core Competencies; consider keeping the detail here and shortening the core competency.
- Avoid overstating editing/production if recent roles emphasize strategy and team leadership more than hands-on execution.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution” and “Core Competencies.” This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent platforms or removed.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize recent, proven platforms first: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages”
- Drop GitHub Pages unless you’ve used it materially in recent roles; it feels lighter than the others and may dilute enterprise credibility.
- If space allows, add brief proficiency framing instead of a bare list: “Enterprise CMS: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages”
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; if Drupal is your flagship platform, place it first and consider bolding only if formatting supports it globally.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same platforms plus modernization and technical execution.
- “Web & CMS administration” also appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating the same idea three times.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Make it tighter, more current, and oriented toward implementation depth rather than repeating core web basics.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Technical Implementation & Web Operations
- Reorder by relevance/recency: Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • JavaScript • HTML/CSS
- Collapse dated/basic terms: replace “HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery” with “JavaScript, HTML/CSS” unless jQuery is specifically required for target roles
- If accurate, add scope/context instead of pure tools: “API integrations, serverless scripting, deployment automation, tag management, front-end troubleshooting”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; use this section for tools/platforms only or remove repeated items there
- “Workflow automation” in Topline Skills may overlap with GitHub Actions; keep one framed broadly and the other as a specific tool

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with stronger “workflow/systems” language elsewhere. Make it more selective and frame tools by function to reinforce recent automation/process leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools
- Group by use case instead of one long list: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier • Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp • Slack, Microsoft Teams
- Cut weaker/older tools unless actively used in recent roles; keep the list to the platforms most relevant to NACo consulting/director work
- If space allows, add a light qualifier for impact: “Used to build editorial workflows, automate handoffs, and support cross-team coordination”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating those exact phrases here
- Collaboration tools like Slack/Teams can feel low-value unless tied to workflow coordination rather than basic communication

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this item is too bare to add much value on its own. It should either signal level of use/administration or be tightened so it complements—rather than repeats—the strong email leadership already shown in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename for clarity and scope: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- If accurate, add level/context: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (campaign automation, segmentation)** • **Higher Logic (member email/community engagement)** • **Mailchimp (newsletter deployment)**
- Keep the list to platforms you used meaningfully in recent roles; if one was only light exposure, remove it.
- Standardize naming: use **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys** for current Microsoft branding.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with repeated email/newsletter references in NACo roles; avoid restating newsletter management here.
- If space is tight, this could be folded into a broader **Communications Platforms** line with CRM/CMS tools to reduce fragmentation.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to foundational team-building and production contributions.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh size/timeline, livestream volume, weekly video cadence, audience reach, or production improvements.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce generic terms like “high-impact” and “strengthening”; replace with actions and results.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and standardize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day supervision to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; if kept here, frame this item as launching or piloting the format.
- Website/workflow language also appears in later roles; keep this entry focused on early buildout and hands-on production.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo multimedia/digital work. Emphasize cross-functional coordination and the launch outcome, while keeping it leaner than more recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched the organization’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a more specific verb: “produced” or “supported production of digital and multimedia content for program and policy communications.”
- If possible, add scope or result: number of episodes, audiences served, internal stakeholders supported, or how the podcast/content advanced member engagement.
- Keep this entry shorter than later NACo roles to preserve recency weighting.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production” repeats strongly with later video/studio roles; avoid overexplaining production tasks here.
- Don’t restate broad digital leadership themes already covered in 2018–2024 entries.
